summary.title: Penetration Testing Tools Cheat Sheet
summary.one_liner: A quick-reference list of common penetration testing commands, mainly for infrastructure and network testing, covering recon, enumeration, password attacks, pivoting and exploitation.
keywords: hydra brute force ftp pop3 smtp
how do i enumerate smb shares
how do i pivot through ssh
takeaways: Recon steps include WHOIS, dig lookups and zone transfers, SimplyEmail, and nmap scans with guidance on scan speed (slow scans for external tests).
Service-specific enumeration commands are covered for SMB, SNMP, RSH, finger, Oracle and MSSQL, including Metasploit modules.
Attack and post-exploitation techniques include LLMNR/NBT-NS poisoning with Responder, IKE VPN PSK cracking, SSH and Meterpreter pivoting, and Oracle privilege escalation.
The page is a reference of commands rather than a full guide; it points to man pages and other cheat sheets for detail.
summary.summary: This is a condensed cheat sheet of commands used on typical infrastructure and network penetration tests, with web application testing only touched on briefly. It is organised by phase: pre-engagement, OSINT, port scanning, service enumeration (SMB, SNMP, Oracle, MSSQL, TLS), password attacks, pivoting, exploit research, and Metasploit and Meterpreter usage. Most entries are short command snippets with brief notes on when each is appropriate. The author suggests consulting man pages or linked specific cheat sheets for more depth.
